title: USAir 1016
summary: DC-9 encountered severe microburst-induced windshear during final approach in thunderstorm over Charlotte. Windshear alert system failed to alert crew due to software discrepancy that lowered sensitivity while flaps in transit. Pilot attempted go-around but aircraft could not climb, descended rapidly and crashed into trees and residential street.
probable_cause: Microburst-induced windshear with contributing factors including crew's failure to recognize windshear quickly, failure to establish proper pitch and engine power during go-around, and software deficiency in windshear alert system.

factors.evidence: microburst generated by thunderstorm over airport caused severe wind shear
severe thunderstorms in vicinity of airport with heavy rain
windshear alert system had software discrepancy that lowered sensitivity while flaps were in transit, alert not provided 8-9 seconds prior to impact
crew failed to recognize wind shear quickly due to alert system error and inadequate weather information
aircraft crashed through airport fence and impacted trees, skidding down residential street

events.text: DC-9 cleared for ILS approach to Runway 18R in heavy rain with severe thunderstorms in vicinity
Tower issued windshear warning on different frequency not heard by Flight 1016
Captain realized serious predicament and ordered go-around, first officer instructed to take it around and go right
Aircraft plummeted toward ground, touched down in field 0.5 miles from runway threshold, crashed through fence and impacted trees
